advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the note-prose label/keyword greps in test_finding_contract / test_negative_boundaries with assertions on runner-consumed structure (e.g. expect labels, criterion ids) rather than author wording.
evidence: assert label in note, f"{c['id']} note missing label {label!r}"
eval_scorers.py:404: "emits_valid_findings": _schema_review_result (validates finding schema only; never reads note prose)
assert "silen" in _text("PORT-N1")  # keyword grep on prose wording (lines 91-98)
advisory.finding: test_finding_contract asserts the presence of author-facing prose labels ('Plan citation:', 'Alternate shape:', 'Causal mechanism:', 'Observable breakage:') inside each fire case's `note` field, and test_negative_boundaries greps note/input prose for keyword tokens ('silen', 'cli', 'explicit', 'standard-library'). The `note` field is runner metadata (eval.py:223 lists 'note' in metadata_keys) that is never consumed by any scorer or validator (the emits_valid_findings scorer at eval_scorers.py:404 only validates finding-set schema). These are change-detector assertions on author wording: rewording a note with no change to eval behavior breaks them.
scenarios: An author rewords a fire-case note (e.g. renames 'Plan citation:' to 'Cited mechanism:') while keeping the case semantically identical — the test fails despite no observable eval-behavior change.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate the committed spec with validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True) (matching test_new_eval_specs.py) so unregistered scorer names and unbalanced dataset/gold_set are caught offline.
evidence: eval.py:280-284: "strict=True additionally enforces that every deterministic scorer name is REGISTERED ... and that the dataset + gold_set are present, balanced, and well-shaped ... the lenient default keeps ... user .rebar/evals specs and unit fixtures working"
Existing convention test_new_eval_specs.py:20: assert ev.validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True) == [], prompt_id
advisory.finding: test_spec_contract validates the committed eval spec with the LENIENT validate_eval_spec(spec) (strict defaults to False), which per the function docstring does NOT enforce deterministic-scorer-name REGISTRATION or dataset/gold_set balance. The test asserts the scorer name literal equals 'emits_valid_findings' but never checks it is a registered scorer (known_scorer_names()). A typo'd or unregistered scorer name would pass every test in this file yet be rejected by the packaged CI discipline gate that runs strict validation.
scenarios: The eval YAML's scorer name is mistyped (e.g. 'emit_valid_findings') or points to an unregistered scorer — the committed corpus is silently broken for the real eval run but the unit suite stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change line 53 to `assert _eval.validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True) == []` and, if desired, add an explicit `assert det[0]['name'] in _eval_scorers.known_scorer_names()`.
